hits.name: Logan Kilpatrick
hits.text:
Today we are rolling out Gemini 4 Argon globally in the Gemini API, to Pro + Ultra in Gemini App, and Ultra subs in Antigravity!

Argon is a huge step forward for Gemini, and a labor of love. This model has been battle tested by over 100,000 people at Google over the last month, with so much new innovation, ambition, and hard work baked into this release. The team has been heads down over the last 6 months working to make this possible across the stack (research, infra, safety, eng, etc).

We rolled the model out to cyber defenders as part of our fairwind program and early access customers over the last 2 weeks, it has been amazing to see and talk to folks who are now using this model daily. Seeing the models writing capability, raw knowledge and persistence for coding, paired with new features like 1M token output when the model needs to work more has gotten me even more excited about our path ahead.

This is just the start of the Gemini 4 era. As you saw with 3.5, 3.6, 3.7, and 3.8 Flash, our iteration speed with Gemini is fast : ) Now with Gemini 4 Argon to work from, I am cannot wait to see the progress continue, and most importantly see what this new model enables for the world. 

This is such a special moment in the arc of technology, as millions of people everyday tackle problems they could never have thought possible before. Gemini 4 Argon was built to help you tackle the hardest problems. I have personally felt this spark with Argon and hope you do too. Onwards!!
hits.hook: Today we are rolling out Gemini 4 Argon globally in the Gemini API, to Pro + Ultra in Gemini App, and Ultra subs in Anti
hits.draft_en:

outsiders.name: Kun Chen
outsiders.text:
let me break down “software is dead” for you

the latest argument is “you just tell your agent what you want, and your agent will vibe code software on the fly to get that done, so no one will need real software any more”

sounds reasonable, until you realize it costs tokens, compute, and wall clock time to build those software on the fly

so instead of one-click launching an app, the bet is people will prefer to write a prompt, wait for 15 minutes, then get something that may or may not do what they want, and at the end of the month pay more $$$ for the token spend, higher than all their software combined

that’s literally the argument

and if we look at the world in aggregate, most people would just end up building the exact same “personal” software repeatedly

oh - your agent just spent 3 days and $500 of tokens vibe coding your terminal multiplexer? mine just did exactly the same! let’s celebrate how personal our terminal multiplexers are!

sorry - i just don’t see that as being a happy scenario for anyone, other than people who profit from telling others how to waste $ on tokens

to be constructive, here’s what i believe as the future state -

- high quality software that takes high cost to make will continue to thrive. just like good restaurants don’t compete with your air fryer and microwave 

- most of those software will be offered headlessly for people to use via their agents, and they can continue to monetize such usage. this is already the case with products like jira, linear, stripe

- human-facing software will all offer dynamic UI that can be adjusted with natural language on the fly so they can be personalized easily, but their core doesn’t have to be rebuilt by every user repeatedly

instead of “software is dead”, i believe good software becomes “strong core, headless service, fluid interface”

which future do you think is more likely?

virals.angle: Muse Wonder made it a three-lab race overnight
virals.inspired_by: @theo rankings 'S: Opus 5.5, Muse Wonder' (1.01M) + Muse 3D take (829k) + bug-fix test (638k) + @ArtificialAnlys index 52/56 (409k) + @AlexFinn 'trained to not give up' (103k)
virals.draft_en:
Meta shipped Muse Wonder and the model rankings changed in a day.

Theo's list hit 1M views: S tier is Opus 5.5 and Muse Wonder. A tier is GPT-6.1 Sol. Then a gap.

His best test: he asked all three to fix the same bug. Opus found the root cause and filed a PR. Sol wrote 300 lines of tests and an explanation nobody could follow. Muse found a PR someone else already filed and said merge that instead.

Run your own three-model bug test this week. Same bug, same prompt. Post what each one did.
virals.video_tip: 12s: three terminal windows side by side labeled Opus, Sol, Muse, each solving the same bug differently, the last one just pointing at an existing PR, caption the laziest fix won.

virals.inspired_by: @AlexFinn Grok Bot $500 sponsor (158k) + @levelsio 'get rich helping IRL businesses automate' (222k) + Yohei autonomous research $114 compute (6.5k)
virals.draft_en:
Alex Finn's agent built a site, shipped 40+ PRs, grew a 1,500-person newsletter, made a Stripe link and sold a $500 sponsorship. He ran the social posts. That's it.

The same day, Pieter said the fastest money in AI is walking into normal businesses and automating them.

Two routes, one idea: point an agent at a real problem and let it run the boring parts.

Give your agent a $1 goal this week. One niche you know, one way to charge. Track what it does on its own.
virals.video_tip: 10s: a counter going $0, $1, $500 while a list of agent actions scrolls past, caption the agent did the work, I did the posts.

virals.angle: Software isn't dead, it's going headless
virals.inspired_by: @kunchenguid 'strong core, headless service, fluid interface' (86k) + @levelsio 'close to dead' (55k) + @iamgingertrash hardware over IP (24k) + @gregisenberg chauffeur computers (62k)
virals.draft_en:
The best answer to 'software is dead' came from Kun Chen, 86k views.

Vibe coding your own tools costs tokens, compute and time. Most people would just rebuild the same 'personal' terminal multiplexer for $500 each.

His version of the future: strong core, headless service, fluid interface. Good software keeps its core, agents use it through an API, and humans reshape the UI with words.

Ask one question about your product today: could an agent use it without ever opening the UI? If not, that's your roadmap.
virals.video_tip: 10s: an app's UI peeling away to reveal an API core, an agent plugging in, then the UI reforming in a new layout from a voice command, caption strong core, fluid interface.
